title: Segregated restaurants, the Dallas streetcar sign, passing between sections
summary: Moore tells how he could go in either section, and the Dallas streetcar sign episode.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
with, say, musicians even trying to get gas or being late for a gig, running into difficulties of what-have-you?

The worst times -- in restaurants they always had a colored section and a white section and most of the times, a lot of the times they would ask me to go in and get the sandwiches and they wouldn't know what to do, they wouldn't know how to take me whether I was a white or colored, and at one time on the streetcars in Dallas when you get in the streetcar they have a slot there and there's a piece of wood -- on one side it says "White" on the other side it says "Colored." So if there's space in the back and there's a place, you had to lift up that sign and put it back in order to get to the place where the colored section is. So I got tired of doing that one time and I just sat down when I got on the streetcar. A guy kept looking at me, he kept looking at me and I kept looking back at him. Anyhow he figured that I was what I was. So that's just one of the few experiences I have had. Rather than continue in that vein, I'd rather go back into the colored section because I can go in either section. I don't want to go through this trauma, I'm a full-blooded American, I didn't want to brag about it.
